newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS CHIEF DESIGNER TO JOIN MCLAREN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS CHIEF DESIGNER TO JOIN MCLAREN.

text.p: Chief designer Adrian Newey, who fell out with the Williams team late last year over a contractual dispute, is to join Formula One rivals McLaren on August 1, it was announced on Tuesday.
In two separate but identical statements, the Williams and McLaren teams confirmed the long awaited news in Formule One circles. Newey had been on "leave' from Williams all this year.

Newey will join McLaren as the Mercedes-Benz-powered team's technical director and will be expected to help accelerate the Woking-based team's recovery from several years in the doldrums during which their chassis have often been criticised.

Following the departure of engine suppliers Honda from Formula One at the end of 1992, McLaren have been struggling to regain their winning form of the late 1980s and early 1990s before Williams began their own spell of supremacy.

Newey, regarded as a gifted aerodynamicist, has been seen as one of the biggest reasons for Williams domination -- they have won the constructors' championship with Renault power four times in the last five years.

His dispute with Williams developed during 1996 when, it was believed, he disagreed with the team's decision to dispose of the services of Briton Damon Hill, who won the world drivers' title for the team that season.

It was understood also that Newey wished to have both greater control over the technical side of the team -- which has been under the guidance of technical director Patrick Head for many years -- and a louder voice on racing matters, including the selection of drivers.
Newey and Williams were prepared to go to court to settle their difference over conflicting interpretations of clauses in Newey's contract of employment.

Newey is also one of the Williams staff named and charged with manslaughter in connection with the death of Brazilian triple world champion Ayrton Senna at Imola, during the San Marino Grand Prix, in 1994.
This year's San Marino Grand Prix takes place at Imola this weekend.
